newsitem.title: INDIA: India's ECL sees Punjab phone licence by Aug 31.
newsitem.headline: India's ECL sees Punjab phone licence by Aug 31.

text.p: India's Essar Commvision Ltd (ECL) will sign a fixed-line telephone licence for the state of Punjab by August 31, a company spokesperson said on Monday.
ECL is 90-percent owned by the Essar group and 10 percent by Bell Atlantic Corp. It was formed in 1995 to bid for rights to start a network in Punjab, one of India's most prosperous states.
But ECL ran into problems with the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) over payment of bank guarantees for a licence.
This year, the DoT tried to remove ECL from a shortlist of companies considered for fixed-line licences, and ECL countered by filing suit against the DoT.

"The Department of Telecommunications has given us until August 31, as we have withdrawn a civil suit against them. We are putting our financing in place, and hope to sign the licence before August 31," an ECL spokeswoman told Reuters.
She said ECL would pay 1.31 billion rupees ($36.6 million) for the first year licence fee and place 750 milion ruppees in bank guarantees by August 31.
She also denied reports in The Observer of Business and Politics daily newspaper that Bell Atlantic was quitting the joint venture.
"They are our partner and will stay in the consortium for at least five years," she said.
She said the Essar group had asked Bell Atlantic to increase its ECL stake to 30 percent, but the American company decided not to in the wake of U.S. telecommunications deregulation.
ECL plans to invest $1 billion in Punjab over the next three years to install 525,000 lines.
It recently signed a deal worth $5 million with Motorola Inc for a hybrid cable pilot project to deliver voice, video and data to 2,000 households.
The deal has the potential to involve 200,000 homes, an ECL official said when announcing the agreement, with each line worth around $1,000.
